items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline. Softer and warmer on the quote 'Wars end... but neighbours remain.'
lines: Narrator
You're looking at a country that's survived about seventeen hundred years, right in the middle of Italy.
Narrator
It even turned down free land from Napoleon.
Narrator
This is San Marino. Just sixty-one square kilometres. About half the size of Paris.
Narrator
And Italy has two countries inside it. The other is the Vatican, the smallest on Earth.
Narrator
So how does something this tiny stay free, surrounded on every side?
Narrator
Rewind to three oh one. The story goes, a stonemason named Marinus climbed this mountain and started a tiny community.
Narrator
Fifteen centuries later, Napoleon is marching through Italy. He likes San Marino... and offers to make it bigger.
Narrator
Their leader's reason? Wars end... but neighbours remain.
Narrator
And it's believed that saved them. When Napoleon fell, they had no land to give back.
Narrator
Then in eighteen forty-nine, they hid Garibaldi, a hero of Italy's unification, from an Austrian army.
Narrator
So when Italy came together, San Marino was allowed to stay free.
Narrator
Here's the twist. The best way to survive next to a giant... is to never want its land.
Narrator
They even made Abraham Lincoln an honorary citizen, in eighteen sixty-one.
Narrator
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
